title: Per-layer entropy-aware KV calibration and runtime precision gating for INT8/FP8
creator: Ava Chen
description: Run a targeted experiment that (1) calibrates per-layer KV cache quantization parameters using an entropy-aware objective, (2) validates INT8 and FP8 profiles across diverse workloads, and (3) evaluates a lightweight runtime precision gating mechanism that selects per-request per-layer precision to balance p99 latency and downstream quality. Goal: find a deployment-ready calibration + gating configuration that reduces token cost/latency for conversational workloads while keeping end-user quality regressions within acceptable bounds.
acceptance_criteria: INT8 or FP8 KV profiles produce >=18% median token-cost reduction vs fp16 baseline on our conversational sample suite
p99 tail latency reduction >=10% without increasing p50 by more than 5% on small/medium sequence workloads
End-to-end quality regression <=0.8% measured on the core eval set (mix of perplexity, response-quality scoring, and hallucination detectors)
Runtime precision gating must choose lower precision for >=35% of requests on average and maintain SLA for high-priority customers
Calibration pipeline reproducible (deterministic seed + saved artifacts) and documented in Confluence with runbook for retuning
steps: Define evaluation workloads: baseline conversational set (10k prompts), adversarial holdout (1k), latency stress tests (burst patterns)
Implement per-layer entropy scoring: histogram-based entropy + KLD drift detector on KV activations
Calibrate per-layer scales for INT8 and FP8 using L2 + entropy regularization and compare against uniform min-max and percentile methods
Instrument runtime gating prototype: lightweight heuristics (prefix length, token variance) + fallback policy to full precision on quality signals
Run large-scale A/B: baseline fp16 vs INT8 profile vs FP8 profile vs gated hybrid (7-day runs) across dev fleet with synthetic traffic
Collect metrics: token-cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, quality suite (automatic scoring + sampled human labels), error rates, and memory/KV hit ratios
Analyze false-positive quality drops and rollback rules; produce candidate policy for rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%)
Document pipeline and package calibration artifacts for ops to consume (tarball of per-layer scales, metadata, and expected drift thresholds)
notes: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting with infra and runtime leads. Decided to prioritize entropy-aware calibrator over naive percentile for initial sweep (Ava)
2025-02-13: Prototype per-layer entropy scorer implemented. Early results show entropy correlates with sensitivity to quantization in later layers (Diego)
2025-02-15: Initial INT8 calibration reduced median token cost by ~15% but exhibited 1.6% regression on hallucination metric for adversarial holdout; exploring gating thresholds
2025-02-17: FP8 profiles show smoother quality curve but less latency improvement; gating prototype selected lower precision for ~30% of requests under default thresholds
2025-02-18: Decided to add a small human-label holdout for critical customer intents before canary rollout. Ops asked for a rollback token counter in console (linked task created)
implementation_notes: Keep calibration runs deterministic by pinning RNG seeds; persist per-layer stats and add drift detectors that trigger automated recalibration when KLD > threshold. Use cross-check on cached vs non-cached generation to ensure gating does not introduce prefix-specific artifacts.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: INT8 causes subtle semantic drift on long-prefix examples -> Mitigation: conservative gating for requests with long prefix and human-review holdout
Risk: Calibration overfits to synthetic training prompts -> Mitigation: include production trace samples and adversarial holdout in calibration cost
Risk: Ops complexity in deploying per-layer artifacts -> Mitigation: bundle a verification script and add CI gate to runtime that validates artifact checksums before load
